cards.explanation: The answer is gift. Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters AND a gift to Hezekiah (2 Kings 20:12). Getting mail with a present attached is a good day for anybody, friends. I'd open that one first.

The answer is that he heard Hezekiah had been ill. Merodach-baladan sent letters and a gift "…for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness." (2 Kings 20:12) Word travels, even to a distant land, friends. Nothing else is listed as the cause.

The answer is everything in his palace and kingdom. The text says "There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them." (2 Kings 20:13) Silver, gold, spices, oil, armory, storehouses, the whole lot, friends. That's a tour with no skipped rooms.

The answer is True. The armory is right there in the list: "…as well as his armory…" (2 Kings 20:13) Silver, gold, spices, oil, and the place where the weapons were kept, friends. Hezekiah showed the envoys all of it.
The answer is False. Hezekiah answers Isaiah, "They came from a distant land… from Babylon." (2 Kings 20:14) Close by it was not, friends. Isaiah asked a direct question and he got a direct answer.

The answer is False. The LORD says everything in the palace and all that Hezekiah's fathers had stored up will be carried off to Babylon, and then He says, "Nothing will be left…" (2 Kings 20:17) Not a few left behind, friends, and not a single cookie crumb of treasure.

The answer is Babylon. That's the same place those envoys came from, friends. The LORD says everything in the palace "…will be carried off to Babylon." (2 Kings 20:17) The visitors had seen it all, and now Isaiah says where it's going.

The answer is descendants. Isaiah says, "…some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon." (2 Kings 20:18) Friends, I think this is the heavy part of the word. It's not only about treasure anymore.

The answer is that Hezekiah says the word of the LORD is good. He tells Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." (2 Kings 20:19) It's a surprising thing to say right after hearing that, friends. The rest of that verse tells us what he was thinking.

The answer is that he's thinking there will be peace in his lifetime. The text says, "For he thought, “Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?”" (2 Kings 20:19) That's the thought the verse gives right alongside his reply, friends. It's the thought behind the words he says to Isaiah.

The answer is True. The verse says Hezekiah "…constructed the pool and the tunnel to bring water into the city…" (2 Kings 20:20) A pool and a tunnel, friends. That's a lot of digging, and I'd have needed a very long mustache.

The answer is Manasseh. The verse says, "…his son Manasseh reigned in his place." (2 Kings 20:21) Hezekiah rested with his fathers, friends, and the throne passed to his son. That wraps up the story of Hezekiah.
